This paper introduces the Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with eXogenous covariates (TV-PARX) model, a new framework that captures nonlinear series characteristics and allows for dynamic changes in regression relationships. The TV-PARX model can be viewed as extending Time-Varying Bayesian Neural Networks, particularly for positive and count data, and is further distinguished from similar approaches by its ability to cope with structural breaks and nonlinear dynamics. The paper also outlines an efficient computation method for TV-PARX, deviates from the conventional Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach, promotes the use of a Metropolis-Hastings within Gibbs sampler, and advocates for using TV-PARX in combination with time-varying covariates to analyze series characteristics. A simulation study was conducted to evaluate the performance of TV-PARX, explore its capabilities in dealing with nonlinear series features and adaptive alteration patterns, and explore the impact of structural breaks on the model. The study found that the TV-PARX model consistently outputs accurate results and outperforms the Time-Varying Bayesian Neural Network model across multiple nonlinear series scenarios. The results also indicate that the model can effectively detect structural breaks and nonlinear dynamics in time series data. A real-world application of the TV-PARX model was also explored, analyzing the time-varying relationships between COVID-19 cases and vaccination rates in 30 US states. The study found varying levels of vaccine effectiveness across different states and time periods, and identified possible structural breaks in the series data. The findings suggest that the TV-PARX model can be a powerful tool for analyzing complex time series data and providing valuable insights into nonlinear series features and adaptive alteration patterns.
